data.title: META Stock Breaks Out of Triangle: Elliott Wave Points to New Highs
data.description:
Meta is doing pretty well, and not only that, it has outperformed its own sector by more than 20% over the last two months or so.

It has also outperformed the S&P 500 by more than 17%, which is quite impressive, especially if we consider that the communication services sector has been lagging a bit, although not as much as some other sectors like industrials, materials, and financials. Of course, energy and technology are in a league of their own this year.

But overall, if the communication services sector also starts to pick up, then we can expect Meta, which is already performing very well, to extend even higher.

Meta vs sector and S&P 500 relative strength

In fact, looking at this stock from an Elliott Wave perspective, we can see that the price has broken out of the recent triangle, which looks like it could be completed. Price recovered towards $700, and we saw a very sharp and strong recovery. So after some pullback, which could already be playing out now, we could see even more gains. What I would be looking for is support around $692, the previous breakout point. If more aggressive selling occurs in the near term, then $712 is also an important level to watch, as it marks an unfilled gap from mid-September.

Meta daily Elliott Wave chart

So it’s very possible that we will see another push higher in the next few weeks, but who knows, maybe we will have to wait until the next earnings release, scheduled for Wednesday, October 28. Overall, this looks like a bullish, constructive pattern, and new highs could still be coming in wave five, closer to $850, maybe even $900, as long as the market trades above the $500 level.

Highlights:

  • Meta outperforming its sector by more than 20% and the S&P 500 by over 17% in the last two months
  • Elliott Wave triangle appears completed, with a strong bullish breakout
  • Watching support near $692 and the mid-September gap around $712
  • Next earnings release scheduled for October 28
  • Potential wave five targets around $850–900
  • Bullish outlook remains valid above $500

data.title: AMD Elliott Wave: Tracking a Complex Wave Four Pullback
data.description:
AMD (Advanced Micro Devices) slowed down recently after we identified five waves up with an extended wave three, so we are now tracking a wave four pullback. We think this correction could become a bit more complex and longer in time — especially when we compare it with wave two of the same degree.

In Elliott Wave Theory, fourth waves often take more time and develop more sideways or overlapping structure than second waves.

That is why patience matters here: the 38.2% or even the 50% retracement can still be retested, particularly if we consider the open gap around the 360–394 area.

If you are looking to join the broader uptrend later, that support zone is a much better place to watch for potential rebound opportunities — while the bullish structure remains valid with AMD trading above the 267 invalidation level.

Quick reminder: in a five-wave impulse, wave four is the corrective pause after a strong wave three. It should not break the end of wave one (here reflected by the 267 invalidation).

Until that level holds, the larger count still points to a later wave five advance once wave four completes. For more analysis visit us at wavetraders.com and apply for 7 day free access.

data.title: Gold Rally Reaches Up Near Top of “Cup” Formation
data.description:
Gold and silver prices have rallied sharply off the recent lows.

While there is no guarantee that this is anything more than a “bounce,” it is of interest to note the price formation on Gold. In particular, the Gold ETF (GLD) which is today’s featured chart.

What makes this chart so interesting is the way that it built a “cup” formation basing pattern. The right side of the cup has been built by the steady, persistent rally.

Price is now approaching the top of the cup formation (resistance). It is likely that we will see some consolidation or pulling back from there. How this takes shape will be important. Bulls want to see consolidation or a minor pullback (that leads to a breakout). BUT if we retrace more that 50 percent of the rally, then we are likely back to the sideways base building again (that will take more time before any breakout).

data.title: Financial Sector ETF (XLF): Cup (and Maybe Handle) Watch
data.description:
The Financial Sector has been strong for the past 4 months, rallying back to test its 2026 high.

This trading pattern has resulted in a very broad base that resembles a “cup” formation. This is a potentially bullish formation that often leads to a “handle” (cup with handle is the most bullish form of this basing pattern). The handle forms in a consolidation phase.

While there’s not enough price action to say a handle has formed, XLF is testing its highs and a breakout here would be bullish for the sector as well as the broader market.

Not sure if we see some further consolidation resembling a handle, but it’s safe to say that bulls should add XLF to their watch list.

data.title: Retail Sector ETF (XRT) Trading Near Top Of Price Range
data.description:
The performance of the Retail Sector is a nice barometer for the economy. And the Retail Sector ETF (XRT) is currently trading into important price resistance.

This resistance is formed between $89 and 92.50, levels that have been tested 6 times over the past 10 months.

As you can see in today’s featured chart, this level also marks the top of a 10 month price range.

A breakout here would be very bullish for the sector, while offering a bullish data point about the economy. Stay tuned.
